reason: The filing adds a new service obligation to Airbus and other buyers of divested Spirit businesses, a counterparty and source of loss absent from last year's text.

evidence: unforeseen technical difficulties that could delay project start-up, incur or escalate costs, or cause unscheduled project downtime
reason: Adds cost consequences to an existing technical-difficulty risk and minor wording, but does not describe the exposure as larger, more likely, or already happening.

title: Operational efficiency.
label: boilerplate
evidence: successfully integrate and achieve the anticipated synergies of acquisitions. This requires
reason: This year drops the named Pioneer acquisition reference and condenses the text, but the operational efficiency exposure and its substance are unchanged.

title: Research and development and technological change.
label: boilerplate
evidence: such as AI, including successfully applying advances in the ability to process and integrate large amounts of data to our businesses and decision-making processes
reason: Naming AI and adding decision-making and the 'both nationally and internationally' scope are wording expansions of a technology already covered; no new source of loss or escalation of exposure is described.

title: Safety, business controls, and risk management.
label: boilerplate
evidence: potential risks related to new energy and other technologies
reason: Changes are rewording and a title edit; the added phrase 'other technologies' is vague and does not clearly introduce a new source of loss.

title: Competition.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Technology and expertise provided by industry service companies or AI may also enhance the competitiveness of firms
reason: AI is newly named as a competitive technology that could lift rivals lacking ExxonMobil's resources, a source of competitive loss not covered last year.

title: We are subject to a variety of new, existing, and changing laws and regulations worldwide that could harm our business, and will likely be subject to an even broader scope of laws and regulations as we continue to expand our business.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The scope of the text and data mining exception is being challenged before courts in the EU, which could harm some aspects of our business.
reason: A pending EU court challenge to the text and data mining exception is a new, specific source of potential business harm not described last year.

title: We face intense competition across all markets for our products and services, which could adversely affect our results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Our AI offerings compete with AI products from hyperscalers, open-source offerings, and frontier model providers, some of which are also current or potential partners.
reason: This year adds explicit competition from hyperscalers, frontier model providers, and partners in AI offerings, a counterparty type not named before, though AI competition was already covered last year.

title: Cyberattacks and security vulnerabilities could lead to reduced revenue, increased costs, liability claims, or harm to our reputation or competitive position.
label: new_exposure
evidence: code generated by AI could include errors, deficiencies, or vulnerabilities that increase our exposure to cyberattacks
reason: Adds AI-generated code as a new source of product vulnerabilities, which last year's text did not cover, though AI features were already mentioned.

title: Abuse of our platforms may harm our reputation or user engagement.
label: new_exposure
evidence: certain AI technologies, including conversational or emotionally engaging AI systems, may present distinct risks for children and adolescents
reason: This year adds conversational and emotionally engaging AI systems and age-assurance obligations for app stores and operating systems, which last year's child-safety text did not cover.

title: We are subject to a variety of new, existing, and evolving legal and regulatory requirements that could adversely affect our results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: governments may impose restrictions on the development, deployment, availability, or cross-border access to advanced AI models based on safety, cybersecurity, or national security
reason: The AI section now flags possible government restrictions on availability and cross-border access to advanced AI models, a source of loss last year's text did not cover.

title: The expiration or loss of patent protection and licenses, including the loss of exclusivity for any of our products and increased competition from generics and biosimilars, may adversely affect AbbVie's revenues and operating earnings.
label: de_escalated
evidence: AbbVie anticipates such loss will continue to cause a significant decline in Humira's revenue
reason: This year's text drops the Humira biosimilar competition and the anticipated significant revenue decline, and the top-product share falls from 47% to 42%, a material driver removed.

title: AbbVie is subject to cost-containment efforts and pricing pressures that could cause a reduction in revenues and operating earnings, and changes in the terms of rebate and chargeback programs, which are common in the pharmaceuticals industry, could have a material adverse effect on AbbVie's operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: In January 2026, Botox was selected as one of 15 medicines subject to government-set prices
reason: Botox is newly subject to IRA government-set prices from 2028, a product exposure not covered last year; MFN and reference-pricing risks are also newly described.

title: New products and technological advances by AbbVie's competitors may negatively affect AbbVie's results of operations.
label: boilerplate
evidence: therapeutic areas such as immunology, neuroscience, oncology and aesthetics
reason: Only the list order of therapeutic areas changed and eye care was dropped; the competitive exposure itself is unchanged, so this is not material.

title: Laws and regulations affecting government benefit programs could impose new obligations on AbbVie, require it to change its business practices, and restrict its operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The 340B Drug Pricing Program requires participating manufacturers to offer discounts to covered entities and growth in entities claiming entitlement to 340B pricing has increased the portion of our sales subject to such discounts.
reason: This year adds a new 340B discount exposure and related enforcement and litigation risk that last year's text did not discuss, though 340B was already named as a regulation.

title: AbbVie depends on information technology and a failure of, or significant disruption to, those systems, or a failure to adequately adopt emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, could have a material adverse effect on AbbVie's business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The healthcare and biopharmaceutical industries remain targets of cybersecurity threats due to the value and sensitivity of the data they hold.
reason: Risk is substantively unchanged: the same cyber exposure and consequences are described, with only the industry wording and the removed 'to date' reassurance altered.

title: Abbott may acquire other businesses, license rights to technologies or products, form alliances, or dispose of or spin-off businesses, which could cause it to incur significant expenses and could negatively affect profitability.
label: boilerplate
evidence: the expected benefits may not be realized or may not be realized within the expected time period
reason: Adds a timing qualifier to benefit risk and rewords intangibles phrasing; no new source of loss or change in exposure size, so boilerplate.

title: Abbott will incur additional indebtedness in connection with the Exact Sciences acquisition, which could adversely affect its business, including decreasing its business flexibility.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Abbott plans to fund the Exact Sciences acquisition with approximately $20 billion of borrowings
reason: The planned $20 billion acquisition financing is a new source of debt-related risk that last year's text did not cover, a material increase in indebtedness.

title: It is costly for Abbott to comply with numerous governmental regulations and to develop compliant products and processes, and consequences for non-compliance could have a material adverse effect on Abbott's revenues, profitability, cash flows, and financial condition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: regulations regarding manufacturing practices, testing requirements, product labeling
reason: The added "testing requirements" falls under the same existing FDA regulation; other changes are hyphenation and dropping a cross-reference, with no change in substance.

title: The expiration or loss of intellectual property protection and licenses may affect Abbott’s future revenues and operating earnings.
label: boilerplate
evidence: governments may also challenge or diminish intellectual property protections
reason: Changes are wording tweaks ("diminish", "operating earnings") and removal of a cross-reference to Legal Proceedings; no change in substance of exposure.

title: Changes in geopolitical and macroeconomic conditions could negatively affect Abbott’s business, financial condition, and results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: The U.S. government has imposed tariffs on imports into the U.S., and it may impose additional tariffs in the future.
reason: Tariff risk was already covered but is now described as actually imposed, with retaliation and supply chain disruption also named, so the exposure has materialised.

title: New products and technological advances by Abbott’s competitors may negatively affect Abbott’s results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: including disruptive technologies such as artificial intelligence
reason: Artificial intelligence is newly named as a disruptive technology that could change competitive dynamics, a source of competitive risk not previously covered.

title: Other factors can have a material adverse effect on Abbott’s future profitability and financial condition.
label: new_exposure
evidence: additional challenges of doing business internationally, including differing local product preferences and product requirements, difficulty in establishing, staffing, and managing operations, and differing labor regulations
reason: This year's text adds a new international-operations risk factor not present last year, a distinct source of loss covering foreign business challenges.

title: Our results of operations have been, and may in the future be, adversely affected by volatile, negative or uncertain economic and geopolitical conditions and the effects of these conditions on our clients’ businesses and levels of business activity.
label: escalated
evidence: including the ongoing conflict in the Middle East
reason: Geopolitical tensions were already covered, but the text now cites a specific ongoing conflict as a concrete, current source of adverse impact, which is a new example of harm already materialising.

title: Our business depends on generating and maintaining client demand for our solutions and services, including through the adaptation and expansion of our solutions and services in response to ongoing changes in technology and offerings, and a significant reduction in such demand or an inability to respond to the evolving technological environment could materially affect our results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: For example, limited client technology budgets may be increasingly allocated to AI investments which may reduce client spending on, or demand for, certain of our solutions and services.
reason: Adds a concrete AI budget-reallocation mechanism reducing demand, and states that industry developments have in the past shifted demand, showing the risk is already materialising.

title: Risks and uncertainties related to the development and use of AI, including advanced AI, could harm our business, damage our reputation or give rise to legal or regulatory action.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Many of our AI solutions and services rely on third-party AI models, platforms and infrastructure providers over which we have limited control
reason: Reliance on third-party AI models, platforms and infrastructure is a new dependency source of loss that last year's text did not cover.

title: If we are unable to match people and their skills with client demand around the world and attract and retain professionals with strong leadership skills, our business, the utilization rate of our professionals and our results of operations may be materially adversely affected.
label: escalated
evidence: legislative, regulatory or executive actions have and may in the future increase the cost of obtaining or maintaining H-1B or similar visas in the U.S. or require us to pay higher wages to visa holders
reason: Last year's H-1B risk was hypothetical; this year says visa rule changes have already raised costs and wages, so the existing exposure is now materialising.

title: We face legal, reputational and financial risks from any failure to protect client and/or Accenture data from security incidents or cyberattacks.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The rapid development and increasing use of AI technologies, including autonomous or semi-autonomous agents, within our and our clients’ businesses have created new attack surfaces, security vulnerabilities
reason: Last year's text covered AI only as a threat-actor tool; this year adds the company's own AI and autonomous agents as a new source of attack surface and loss.

title: The markets in which we operate are highly competitive, and we might not be able to compete effectively.
label: de_escalated
evidence: AI, software, platform, cloud migration and other solutions that may require integration services to a lesser extent
reason: Adding 'may' hedges the claim that AI and platform offerings reduce demand for integration services, softening the stated threat. The added AI-native and software competitors fall under the existing start-up category.

title: If we do not accurately anticipate the cost, risk and complexity of performing our work or if third parties upon whom we rely do not meet their commitments, then our contracts could have delivery inefficiencies and be less profitable than expected or unprofitable.
label: boilerplate
evidence: many of our contracts tie our compensation to agreed-upon performance standards, milestones or outcome-based measures such as cost savings, revenue enhancement or business goals
reason: The performance-linked compensation paragraph was condensed and dropped examples of consequences, but the same exposure remains, with no statement that it shrank or ended.

title: Changes in our level of taxes, as well as audits, investigations and tax proceedings, or changes in tax laws or in their interpretation or enforcement, could have a material adverse effect on our effective tax rate, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Ireland has enacted Pillar Two, the OECD’s global minimum tax rate, and other countries where we operate have either enacted Pillar Two or are actively considering changes
reason: Pillar Two was already disclosed last year; this year's edit reorders and rewords the same global minimum tax exposure with no change in substance, the G7 reference being dropped without saying the exposure shrank.

title: Our results of operations could be materially adversely affected by fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Our currency hedging activities are subject to risks related to counterparty performance under hedging contracts
reason: Changes are condensation and an 'off-shore' to 'offshore' spelling fix; the hedging risks remain fully described, so substance is unchanged.

title: As a result of our geographically diverse operations and our strategy to continue to grow in our key markets around the world, we are more susceptible to certain risks.
label: new_exposure
evidence: together with changes in geopolitical relationships, trade restrictions or extraterritorial laws, may reduce our ability to standardize and scale solutions across markets
reason: Trade restrictions, extraterritorial laws and local ownership or control requirements are new sources of loss that last year's sovereignty language did not name.

title: If we are unable to manage the organizational challenges associated with our size, we might be unable to achieve our business objectives.
label: escalated
evidence: As our operating model evolves, including through a network of businesses with varying degrees of operational autonomy, it may become more difficult to maintain consistent standards, manage risks and protect our brand and reputation.
reason: The operating model shift to a network of autonomous businesses is a new structural risk factor that makes standards and risk management harder, extending the existing organizational exposure.

title: We might not be successful at acquiring, investing in or integrating businesses, entering into joint ventures or divesting businesses.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We have paid and in the future may pay higher valuations for acquisitions, particularly for solutions and platforms and assets in areas with significant growth potential and higher demand, which may require longer periods to generate expected returns.
reason: Overpaying for acquisitions, with longer payback periods, is a new cause of loss that last year's risk factor did not mention.

title: Our business could be materially adversely affected if we incur legal liability.
label: de_escalated
evidence: the contracting practices of competitors, along with the demands of increasingly sophisticated clients, may cause contract terms and conditions that are unfavorable to us to become new standards in the industry
reason: This year's filing drops the risk that competitors' contracting practices make unfavorable contract terms industry standard, removing a material driver of contractual liability without saying the risk ended.

title: Our work with government clients exposes us to additional risks inherent in the government contracting environment.
label: escalated
evidence: Government investigations or proceedings related to our diversity, equity and inclusion programs have and may in the future result in financial penalties, sanctions, or restrictions on government contracting
reason: The DEI legal exposure was already covered last year, but this year the company says such proceedings have already resulted in financial penalties, sanctions and contracting restrictions, showing the risk materialising.

title: Our global operations expose us to numerous and sometimes conflicting legal and regulatory requirements, and violation of these regulations could harm our business.
label: de_escalated
evidence: our selection of voluntary disclosure frameworks and standards, and the interpretation or application of those frameworks and standards, may change from time to time or may not meet the expectations of investors or other stakeholders
reason: Last year's text named ESG disclosure-framework and reporting-data risks, including SEC-required disclosures and data revisions; this year drops those drivers, narrowing the exposure.

title: If we are unable to protect or enforce our IP rights, or if our solutions or services infringe upon the IP rights of others or we lose our ability to utilize the IP of others, our business could be adversely affected.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Infringement risk may increase as we expand and deploy AI and deploy software and hardware solutions across multiple clients.
reason: The rewording condenses the text and drops examples such as non-practicing holders, but the company does not say the IP infringement exposure shrank or ended.

title: We may be unsuccessful at innovating in response to rapid technological or industry changes to meet customer needs, which could cause our business and financial results to suffer materially.
label: escalated
evidence: our business and financial results may be materially harmed
reason: Mostly rewording, but the harm is now described as material and agentic AI is added as a named driver, a modest escalation of an existing exposure.

title: We participate in rapidly evolving and intensely competitive markets, and, if we do not compete effectively, our business and financial results could materially suffer.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Other companies have in the past, and may in the future prevent, limit or interfere with our ability to use third-party models in our solutions.
reason: New exposure to third-party model access restrictions; last year's text covered only proprietary rights limiting making, using or selling AI offerings, not third-party model use. Also agentic AI competition is newly named.

title: Issues relating to the development and use of AI in our solutions may result in reputational harm, liability and adverse business and financial results.
label: escalated
evidence: obligations under the EU AI Act have gone into effect
reason: The EU AI Act now applies, with possible administrative fines, and third-party model use is expanded with explicit IP infringement liability, making a covered exposure more concrete and larger.

title: If our reputation or our brands are damaged, our business and financial results may be adversely affected.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Our brands may be negatively affected by the actual or perceived failure to meet our sustainability commitments or appropriately respond to climate concerns
reason: Adds reputational exposure from sustainability commitments and climate concerns, which last year's risk factor did not cover at all.

title: We may not realize the anticipated benefits of acquisitions, investments or other strategic transactions, and they may disrupt our business and adversely affect our business and financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: brand or reputational harm associated with our acquisitions, investments or other strategic transactions
reason: This year's list adds brand or reputational harm from transactions, a source of loss that last year's risk factor did not mention in any form.

title: Service interruptions or failures of our information technology systems or those of third parties may impair the availability of our solutions, which may expose us to liability, damage our reputation and harm our future financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: various business processes such as our enterprise resource planning system and customer and sales support
reason: This year's text adds internal business processes such as the ERP system and customer and sales support as dependencies that could be interrupted, a source of loss not covered last year.</br>

title: Security incidents, improper access to or disclosure of our customers’ data or other cybersecurity incidents may harm our reputation and materially and adversely affect our business.
label: new_exposure
evidence: if our solutions experience a compromise, a large portion or, in some instances, all of our customers and their data for a given solution could be simultaneously affected
reason: The company now flags that a compromise of its solutions in customers' supply chains could simultaneously affect a large portion or all customers, a source of loss not described last year.

title: If we are unable to develop, manage and maintain our sales channels, including our direct sales force, third-party distributors, and sales partners, or third-party relationships upon which we rely for critical business operations, our revenue and business may be adversely affected.
label: boilerplate
evidence: generative AI, large language models, encryption and authentication technology
reason: Adding 'large language models' to an existing example of third-party technology reliance is a clarification, not a new source of loss; other changes are rewording and reordering.

title: We face various risks associated with operating as a multinational corporation, and global adverse economic and geopolitical conditions may harm our business and financial condition.
label: new_exposure
evidence: epidemics and pandemics like COVID-19
reason: Epidemics and pandemics are a new named source of loss not covered in last year's list of risks; tariffs and consumer protection laws fall within already-covered trade and regulatory risks.

title: Some of our enterprise solutions have extended and complex sales cycles, which may increase our costs and make our sales cycles unpredictable.
label: escalated
evidence: particularly for larger and more complex deals
reason: Same enterprise sales-cycle exposure, now with added drivers: agentic AI, regulatory requirements, and geopolitical events like tariffs delaying larger deals, a more concrete source of harm.

title: We are, and may in the future become, subject to litigation, regulatory inquiries, investigations and other actions, which could result in an unfavorable outcome and have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including those initiated by patent assertion entities or competitors
reason: Adds employment practices, investigations and competitors as examples within the same existing litigation and IP-dispute risk; no change in substance or exposure size.

title: We are subject to risks associated with compliance with laws and regulations globally, which may harm our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: sustainability and other regulatory requirements affecting trade and investment
reason: Additions to the list of regulatory areas (sustainability, immigration, government actions, data transfer) are covered by the existing generic regulatory language; no change in described exposure or severity.

title: Increasing regulatory focus on privacy and security issues and expanding laws and regulatory requirements could impact our business models and expose us to increased liability.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We may be subject to certain aspects of the EU’s Digital Services Act, which imposes additional legal requirements on certain types of digital service providers
reason: This year's text adds the EU Digital Services Act and the US DOJ data rule as new legal sources of compliance obligations that last year's text did not mention, introducing new exposure rather than rewording.

title: Our intellectual property portfolio is a valuable asset and we may not be able to protect our intellectual property rights, including our source code, from infringement or unauthorized copying, use or disclosure.
label: boilerplate
evidence: unauthorized disclosure of our source code occurs through security breach, cyber-attack, contributions to open-source projects or otherwise
reason: Open-source contributions are a newly named channel for source code disclosure, but the original "or otherwise" already covered it, so no new source of loss is introduced.

title: Changes in tax rules and regulations or interpretations thereof may adversely affect our effective tax rates.
label: escalated
evidence: Changes in our operating landscape, such as changes in laws or interpretations of tax rules, have in the past and may in the future adversely affect our effective tax rates
reason: The company now states that tax changes have already adversely affected its effective tax rates, showing the risk materialising, while softening 'likely' to 'may' in the same section.

title: Contracting with government entities exposes us to additional risks inherent in the government procurement process.
label: boilerplate
evidence: we are subject to complex regulatory requirements and executive orders, including those related to procurement; export controls; employment; security
reason: Export controls and employment are newly named, but last year's text already covered complex procurement regulations and other government-specific contractual requirements, so no new source of loss appears.

title: If there is a change in subscriptions or renewals in a reporting period, this could cause our financial results to suffer and may not be immediately reflected in our revenue and financial results for that period because we recognize revenue over the subscription term.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Our solutions are typically subscription-based, pursuant to product and service agreements.
reason: Changes are wording swaps (offerings to solutions, product to solution) with the same risk factors, drivers and substance; no new exposure or change in severity.

title: We are subject to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and may not be able to effectively hedge our exposure.
label: de_escalated
evidence: amounts reported as annualized recurring revenue, a performance metric which we measure at currency rates that are set at the beginning of each fiscal year and held constant throughout the year, may vary from actual revenue recognized
reason: Last year's text said constant-currency ARR may diverge from GAAP revenue; this year's omits that driver entirely. Adding 'tariffs' is a new example of already-covered trade disputes, so it is not new exposure.

title: Catastrophic events, including events associated with climate change, may disrupt our business and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: cloud service provider outages
reason: Adds cloud service provider outages as a new disruption source not named last year, though the broader third-party outage risk was already covered, so this is a material new cause of loss.

title: Our stock price has been volatile and your investment could lose value.
label: boilerplate
evidence: changes to our key performance metrics;
reason: The new bullet and other wording changes add examples or rephrase existing stock-price drivers without introducing a new exposure or changing the risk's size.

title: Deterioration of economic conditions, geopolitical tensions, changes in market conditions or weakening global capital markets have affected and may continue to materially affect our businesses, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity.
label: de_escalated
evidence: increased credit risk and decreased sales; and
reason: The inflationary-pressures driver was dropped from the sales-decline bullet, and interest-rate risk language was softened, e.g. 'could in the future increase'.

title: Reinsurance may be unavailable or too expensive relative to its benefit and may not be adequate to protect us against losses.
label: boilerplate
evidence: it makes the reinsurer liable to our subsidiaries for the reinsured portion of the risk
reason: Changes are rewording, dropped qualifiers, cross-reference update, and minor wording on climate and reinsurance mechanics; no change in substance or new exposure.

title: Our consolidated results of operations, liquidity, financial condition and ratings are subject to the effects of natural and man-made catastrophic events as well as mass torts.
label: escalated
evidence: as well as new and emerging mass tort claims, have required and could in the future require us to pay the insured beyond the contractual terms
reason: This year's text adds new and emerging mass tort claims as a driver of inflated claims and drops the 'without regulatory relief' qualifier on capital-ratio impact, making that risk more likely and less conditional.

title: Climate change may adversely affect our business and financial condition.
label: escalated
evidence: Furthermore, claims asserted against insureds have in the past, and may in the future, include alleged failure to manage risks associated with climate change
reason: Claims alleging insureds failed to manage climate risk have already occurred, expanding the existing climate litigation exposure to liability claims that are now materialising.

title: Concentration of our insurance, reinsurance and other risk exposures may have adverse effects.
label: de_escalated
evidence: the deconsolidation for accounting purposes and ongoing divestment of our stake in Corebridge, could increase the materiality of these potential concentrations in the remaining portfolio
reason: This year's text drops last year's Corebridge deconsolidation and divestment driver of concentration risk, a material driver, without replacing it.

title: Our investment portfolio is concentrated in certain segments of the economy, and the performance and value of our investment portfolio are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties.
label: escalated
evidence: Our investment portfolio’s returns have benefited historically from investment opportunities and general market conditions that may not currently exist and may not be repeated.
reason: The new caveat says past favorable returns may not recur, making the existing market-driven valuation risk more likely to hurt returns. Other changes are wording only.

title: We rely on investment management and advisory arrangements with third-party investment managers for the majority of our investment portfolio. The historical performance of any investment manager we engage should not be considered indicative of the future results of our investment portfolio.
reason: no verdict

title: AIG Parent’s ability to access funds from our subsidiaries is limited, and our sources of liquidity may be insufficient to meet our needs, including providing capital that may be required by our subsidiaries.
label: boilerplate
evidence: If AIG Parent is unable to satisfy the required regulatory capital needs of a subsidiary, the subsidiary could become insolvent and be subject to supervisory actions by its regulator
reason: Changes are rewording and reordering: the seizure language became a receiver description and the downgrade sentence moved, with the same underlying risk and no change in exposure size.

title: We may not be able to generate cash to meet our needs due to the illiquidity of some of our investments.
label: new_exposure
evidence: or that limit or restrict, by their terms, our ability to sell or otherwise dispose of such investments
reason: This year's text adds joint ventures and investments with contractual sale restrictions as illiquidity sources that last year's risk factor did not name.

title: A downgrade by one or more of the rating agencies in the Insurer Financial Strength ratings of our insurance companies could limit their ability to write or prevent them from writing new business and impair their retention of customers and in-force business, and a downgrade in our credit ratings could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity.
label: new_exposure
evidence: These events could also trigger regulatory scrutiny and potential actions by our regulators.
reason: A downgrade could now trigger regulatory scrutiny and actions, a source of loss the prior text did not mention. The other edits are wording changes.

title: Our risk management policies, standards and procedures may prove to be ineffective and leave us exposed to unidentified or unanticipated risk, which could adversely affect our businesses, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity.
label: boilerplate
evidence: various jurisdictions have unique requirements with respect to AI, third-party engagement, business resiliency and environmental, social and governance matters as well as matters relating to data protection and cybersecurity
reason: Added regulatory categories and a new underwriting-discipline sentence, but cyber-attacks and AI risks were already covered, so no new source of loss is introduced.

title: Pricing for our products is subject to our ability to adequately assess risks and estimate related losses.
label: boilerplate
evidence: but we may not be able to achieve those returns. Additionally
reason: Wording changes only: the removed 'including due to the factors discussed above' clause still leaves the same listed drivers and risk, and 'push' became 'drive'.

title: We are exposed to certain risks if we are unable to maintain the availability of our critical technology systems and data and safeguard the confidentiality and integrity of our data, which could compromise our ability to conduct business and adversely affect our consolidated business, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity.
label: escalated
evidence: Failure to secure or appropriately handle personally identifiable information or confidential or proprietary information has caused and could in the future cause a loss of data or compromised data integrity.
reason: The prior text said such failures could cause data loss; this year it says they already have, so the risk is shown to be materialising.

title: For additional risks with respect to the use of AI, see Business and Operations – “We are exposed to certain risks if we are unable to maintain the availability of our critical technology systems and data and safeguard the confidentiality and integrity of our data, which could compromise our ability to conduct business and adversely affect our consolidated business, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity,” Regulation – “Our businesses are heavily regulated and changes in laws and regulations may affect our operations, increase our insurance subsidiary capital requirements or reduce our profitability,” and Employees and Competition – “We face intense competition in each of our business lines, and technological changes may present new and intensified challenges to our businesses.” Our foreign operations expose us to risks that may affect our operations.
label: boilerplate
evidence: changes to international trade and/or tariff policies, nationalization and other restrictive government or regulatory actions
reason: Tariff policy is a new example of restrictive government action already covered last year. The added anti-corruption statutes and the geopolitical wording are rewording or renaming with no change in substance.

title: Third parties we rely upon to provide certain business and administrative services on our behalf may not perform as anticipated, which could have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: including potential regulatory consequences, such as increased scrutiny and sanctions
reason: The risk factor adds concrete regulatory consequences (increased scrutiny and sanctions) as possible harms, while the core third-party exposure is otherwise unchanged.

title: We may experience difficulty in marketing and distributing products through our current and future distribution channels and the use of third parties may result in additional liabilities.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including registered representatives, insurance agents and agencies, marketing organizations, business partners, and their respective employees
reason: Adding "business partners" to an existing list of third parties covered by the same liability language is a wording change; the other edits are rewording with no substantive shift.

title: Our restructuring initiatives may not yield expected reductions in expenses and/or improvements in operational and organizational efficiency.
label: boilerplate
evidence: From time to time, we engage in restructuring initiatives designed to reduce our expenses and improve operational and organizational efficiency.
reason: This year adds an introductory sentence and reorders the text, but the substantive risks and drivers are unchanged from last year.

title: Strategic transactions, including business or asset acquisitions and dispositions, may expose us to certain risks.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Strategic transactions, including business or asset acquisitions and dispositions, may expose us to certain risks.
reason: Changes are rewording and broadening of the transaction label; the underlying risks and disclosures are substantively unchanged, with the added 'target' securities mention and dropped 'financial accommodations' example not showing a material shift in exposure.

title: We are subject to risks from our continuing equity market exposure to Corebridge. The anticipated benefits of our sales of Corebridge stock may not be achieved.
label: de_escalated
evidence: the sale of our remaining Corebridge stock involves a number of divestment-related risks
reason: This year's filing drops the paragraph on divestment-related risks (delays, unforeseen losses, valuation challenges) and the tax carryforward consequences, narrowing the disclosed exposure.

title: The Development and Use of AI, including the Company’s Increased AI Solutions and Use of AI Technologies, Could Impact the Long-Term Success of the Company and its Reputation or Give Rise to Legal or Regulatory Action:
label: escalated
evidence: if our AI technologies do not work as intended or produce unexpected outcomes
reason: New explicit risk that AI technologies may fail or produce unexpected outcomes, a more concrete harm pathway than last year's framing, though the core exposure was already covered.

title: Cybersecurity and Data Protection Considerations Could Impact the Company’s Business:
label: de_escalated
evidence: The enactment and expansion of cybersecurity and data protection laws, regulations and standards around the globe
reason: Last year's text named AI laws as a driver of compliance costs; this year drops AI and privacy from the regulatory list, narrowing the named regulatory exposure.

title: We face intense competitive pressures that may harm our operating results.
label: de_escalated
evidence: although the IRS free direct filing system was suspended, proponents of these programs continue to advocate for them
reason: The IRS free direct filing system, previously described as made available with expansion planned, is now stated as suspended, and the consumer tax competition is no longer described as increasing.

title: Future revenue growth depends upon our ability to adapt to technological change and successfully extend our platform, introduce new and enhanced products, features, services and business models.
label: new_exposure
evidence: While we continue to enhance the AI capabilities of our offerings, there can be no assurance that our new or enhanced solutions and AI innovations will be successful, adopted, or monetizable
reason: AI product capabilities and monetization risk are newly described, though last year's text already mentioned AI investments; the added explicit AI offering risk is a new source of loss in substance.

title: Our efforts related to sustainability matters expose us to risks that could adversely affect our reputation and performance.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Sustainability matters continue to be an area of focus for stockholders
reason: Changes are terminology swaps (ESG to sustainability, shareholders to stockholders) and added 'often conflicting' wording; no new exposure, escalation, or de-escalation of substance.

title: Security incidents, improper access to or disclosure of our data or customers’ data, or other cyberattacks on our systems could harm our reputation, business, and financial condition.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Our use of AI in our internal operations and technologies may also create new vulnerabilities or methods of attack.
reason: The company now flags its own internal and product AI use as a new source of vulnerability, which last year's text did not cover; the hybrid-workplace driver was also dropped.

title: A cybersecurity incident affecting the third parties we rely on could expose us or our customers to a risk of loss or misuse of confidential information and significantly damage our reputation.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We cannot guarantee that third parties and infrastructure in our information technology supply chain have not been compromised or that they do not contain exploitable defects or bugs that could result in a breach of our systems and networks.
reason: This year adds a new source of loss: undetected compromise or exploitable defects in the IT supply chain, which last year's text did not cover in this form; the rest is largely wording changes.

title: If we are unable to effectively combat the increasing amount and sophistication of fraudulent activities by malicious third parties, we may suffer losses, which may be substantial, and lose the confidence of our customers and government agencies and our revenues and earnings may be harmed.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Any such fraudulent activities may adversely impact our business.
reason: This year drops the hybrid work model driver, which last year named as heightening the fraud risk; that is a dropped material driver, so de_escalated fits.

title: Business interruption or failure of our information technology and communication systems may impair the availability of our products and services, which may damage our reputation and harm our future financial results.
label: boilerplate
evidence: third-party or cloud computing services and large language models
reason: Large language model providers fall under the existing external service provider exposure, which was already covered. The dropped hybrid workplace example does not show the exposure shrinking.

title: We regularly invest resources to update and improve our internal information technology systems and software platforms. Should our investments not succeed, or if delays or other issues with new or existing internal technology systems and software platforms disrupt our operations, our business could be harmed.
label: new_exposure
evidence: including the integration of AI into our internal operations and technologies
reason: This year's text adds AI integration into internal operations as a new area of investment and disruption risk not covered last year.

title: If we are unable to develop, manage and maintain critical third-party business relationships, our business may be adversely affected.
label: new_exposure
evidence: policies or practices that can affect the visibility or the availability of our offerings
reason: Platform owners' discretion now explicitly reaches offer visibility and availability, not just pricing and terms, and AI platforms are added as distribution channels.

title: Competition for our key employees is intense and we may not be able to attract, retain and develop the highly skilled employees we need to support our strategic objectives.
label: boilerplate
evidence: We may experience higher compensation costs to retain and recruit senior management and highly-skilled employees that may not be offset by improved productivity or revenue.
reason: Only change is removal of the closing sentence 'Other factors may make it more challenging...' and a comma edit; no change in substance of the talent-competition exposure.

title: Uncertainty in the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence in our platform and products and by our customers may result in harm to our business and reputation.
label: escalated
evidence: agentic and generative AI for customers, experts, our workforce, and our internal business operations
reason: Agentic AI and internal business operations are newly named, but they expand the same AI-deployment exposure rather than introducing a new source of loss; added investment-return risk is also new framing, so escalation fits best.

title: If we experience significant product accuracy or quality problems or delays in product launches, it may harm our revenue, earnings and reputation.
label: boilerplate
evidence: as we connect customers to live tax experts and bookkeepers on our platform
reason: The expert-advice risk is the same; the change is rewording and dropped product-name examples, with no change in exposure.

title: Complex and evolving privacy and data protection regulations or changing customer expectations could result in claims, changes to our business practices, penalties or increased cost of operations or otherwise harm our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Regulations related to data privacy, cybersecurity, the collection, processing, storage, transfer and use of data, and the use of AI are evolving and becoming increasingly complex and fragmented.
reason: Changes are mostly wording: added 'increasingly complex and fragmented', AI rules now 'implementing or considering', and the Privacy Shield history dropped, with the same uncertainty still stated and no shrinking of exposure.

title: We are frequently a party to litigation and regulatory inquiries which could result in an unfavorable outcome and have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operation and cash flows.
label: boilerplate
evidence: and the enforcement of priorities of regulatory agencies change
reason: Adds a generic driver of proceedings within an already-covered litigation risk, with no stated increase in likelihood or size; the cross-reference update is also boilerplate.

title: We provide access to capital to small and mid-market businesses and consumers, which exposes us to risk, and may cause us material financial or reputational harm.
label: new_exposure
evidence: and consumers, which exposes us to risk
reason: Consumers are added as a new borrower segment, and new products like business credit cards and fraud risk in applications are introduced, creating exposures not covered last year.

title: Our stock price may be volatile and your investment could lose value.
label: new_exposure
evidence: market trends unrelated to our performance, including perceptions about the impact of evolving technologies, including AI, on our business
reason: This year adds perceptions about AI's impact on the business as a new driver of stock price volatility, which last year's text did not cover.

title: OUR COMMERCIAL LANDSCAPE IS HIGHLY COMPETITIVE, AND CUSTOMERS MAY CHOOSE OUR COMPETITORS’ PRODUCTS OR SERVICES OR MAY NOT ACCEPT ROBOTIC-ASSISTED MEDICAL PROCEDURES, WHICH COULD RESULT IN REDUCED REVENUE AND LOSS OF CUSTOMERS.
label: new_exposure
evidence: academic institutions, governmental agencies, and other public and private research organizations may conduct research, seek patent protection, and establish collaborative arrangements for discovery, research, and marketing of products similar to ours
reason: Academic and government research bodies are a new category of competitor for similar products and talent, not covered in last year's competitor discussion.

title: WE ARE SUBJECT TO A VARIETY OF RISKS DUE TO OUR OPERATIONS OUTSIDE OF THE U.S.
label: escalated
evidence: during 2025, the U.S. federal government imposed new tariffs on imports from various countries including Mexico, Germany, and China
reason: Last year's tariffs were proposed or threatened; this year they were actually imposed on Mexico, where the company manufactures most instruments, so the exposure is now realized.

title: OUR RELIANCE ON SOLE- AND SINGLE-SOURCED SUPPLIERS AND ABILITY TO PURCHASE AT ACCEPTABLE PRICES A SUFFICIENT SUPPLY OF MATERIALS COULD HARM OUR ABILITY TO MEET PRODUCT DEMAND IN A TIMELY MANNER OR WITHIN BUDGET.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the Chinese government announced export controls and licensing requirements applicable to certain products containing Chinese-origin rare earth elements
reason: New Chinese rare earth export controls and licensing requirements create a supply disruption and export-license source of loss that last year's text did not cover.

title: MACROECONOMIC CONDITIONS COULD MATERIALLY ADVERSELY AFFECT OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Certain hospitals have experienced, and may continue to experience, financial and operational pressures as a result of staffing constraints, other labor-related pressures
reason: Changes are rewording and dropped examples (SVB receivership detail, a driver list item) with the same exposures covered; no substantive shift in risk size or new source of loss.

title: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SYSTEM FAILURES, CYBERATTACKS, OR DEFICIENCIES IN OUR CYBERSECURITY COULD HARM OUR BUSINESS, CUSTOMER RELATIONS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: de_escalated
evidence: While, to date, no cyberattacks or security breaches and incidents have had a material impact on our operations or financial results
reason: Prior text said the company is from time to time subject to cyberattacks, treated as ordinary course; this year's text drops that admission and frames past incidents as immaterial, softening the exposure.

title: WE UTILIZE DISTRIBUTORS FOR A PORTION OF OUR SALES AND SERVICE OF OUR PRODUCTS IN CERTAIN COUNTRIES, WHICH SUBJECTS US TO A NUMBER OF RISKS THAT COULD HARM OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: boilerplate
evidence: It may be difficult, expensive, and time-consuming for us to re-establish access or regulatory compliance in such cases.
reason: Changes are rewording and a cross-reference title update; the deleted word 'market' and softened cross-reference wording do not alter the substance of the distributor risk.

title: THE FAILURE TO ATTRACT AND RETAIN KEY PERSONNEL COULD HARM OUR ABILITY TO COMPETE, AND CHANGES IN OUR EXISTING LABOR RELATIONSHIPS COULD MATERIALLY ADVERSELY IMPACT OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The extent and duration of the impact of labor market challenges are subject to numerous factors
reason: Changes are reordering and condensing of labor-risk text plus minor wording edits; the dropped labor-shortage sentence is not a stated shrinkage of exposure, so the less dramatic label applies.

title: INCORPORATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES INTO OUR PRODUCTS, SERVICES, AND OPERATIONS MAY RESULT IN LEGAL AND REGULATORY RISKS OR HAVE OTHER ADVERSE CONSEQUENCES TO OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: escalated
evidence: The cost to comply with such laws, regulations, decisions, and/or guidance interpreting existing laws, or to adjust our business plans based on changes to how such laws are enforced, could be significant and would increase our operating expenses
reason: Regulatory compliance cost was previously described as potentially increasing; it is now described as likely significant and opex-increasing, with new health-AI state laws cited, though the exposure category is unchanged.

title: WE EXPERIENCE LONG AND VARIABLE CONTRACTING CYCLES AND SEASONALITY IN OUR BUSINESS, WHICH MAY CAUSE FLUCTUATIONS IN OUR FINANCIAL RESULTS.
label: boilerplate
evidence: evaluating their robotic-assisted programs to optimize the efficiency of medical procedures using our systems
reason: Changes are rewording and dropping specific product names (da Vinci, Ion) as examples; the contracting-cycle exposure and its drivers are unchanged in substance.

title: THIRD PARTIES MAY OFFER TO SELL REMANUFACTURED OR UNAUTHORIZED INSTRUMENTS AND ACCESSORIES TO OUR CUSTOMERS OR PROVIDE UNAUTHORIZED SERVICE ON OUR SYSTEMS, WHICH COULD ADVERSELY IMPACT SAFETY, OUR FINANCIAL RESULTS, AND OUR REPUTATION.
label: escalated
evidence: the FDA has granted 510(k) clearance for the remanufacturing of certain of these instruments for use with our da Vinci Si, da Vinci X, and da Vinci Xi surgical systems
reason: Remanufacturing was already a covered risk, but FDA clearance now extends to da Vinci X and Xi, which last year's text said had none, widening the realized exposure.

title: OUR BUSINESS IS SUBJECT TO COMPLEX AND EVOLVING LAWS AND REGULATIONS REGARDING DATA PRIVACY, DATA PROTECTION, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AND RESPONSIBLE USE OF DATA, AND ANY FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN SIGNIFICANT LIABILITY, NEGATIVE PUBLICITY, AND/OR EROSION OF TRUST, WHICH MAY ADVERSELY AFFECT OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Any failure, or perceived failure, by us or our vendors to comply
reason: The updated text extends compliance failures to third-party vendors, a counterparty source of loss that last year's text did not name.

title: ONGOING AND FUTURE GLOBAL CONFLICTS COULD ADVERSELY AFFECT OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Disruptions caused by ongoing or future global conflicts, including those resulting from conflicts affecting or in close proximity to countries and regions in the Middle East
reason: This year's text condenses the Israel-Hamas discussion into a generic Middle East conflict reference, and the supply-disruption exposure is still covered, with no change in substance.

title: DISRUPTIONS AT THE FDA AND OTHER GOVERNMENT AGENCIES OR NOTIFIED BODIES COULD PREVENT OUR PRODUCTS FROM BEING CLEARED, CERTIFIED, APPROVED, OR COMMERCIALIZED IN A TIMELY MANNER OR AT ALL, OR COULD HINDER THEIR ABILITY TO PROCURE OUR PRODUCTS, WHICH MAY ADVERSELY AFFECT OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the ability of certain of our government customers to procure our products is subject to appropriations or spending approvals
reason: The filing now flags government customers' procurement being subject to appropriations and shutdowns, a sales-timing and volume risk not covered last year.

title: IF WE DO NOT SUCCESSFULLY MANAGE OUR COLLABORATION, LICENSING, JOINT VENTURE, STRATEGIC ALLIANCE, OR PARTNERSHIP ARRANGEMENTS WITH THIRD PARTIES, WE MAY NOT REALIZE THE EXPECTED BENEFITS FROM SUCH ARRANGEMENTS, WHICH MAY HAVE A MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT ON OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: boilerplate
evidence: following which the Joint Venture began direct distribution operations in China
reason: Only rewording and a dropped product description; the company does not say the exposure shrank, and the rest of the risk text is unchanged.

title: IF WE FAIL TO SUCCESSFULLY ACQUIRE OR INTEGRATE NEW BUSINESSES, PRODUCTS, AND TECHNOLOGY, WE MAY NOT REALIZE EXPECTED BENEFITS, OR OUR BUSINESS MAY BE HARMED.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Failure to successfully integrate our acquisitions may have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, or results of operations.
reason: The only change is removal of the Orpheus Medical example; the risk factor's substance and its general integration exposure are unchanged, so the dropped example is boilerplate.

title: CHANGES IN TAX LAWS OR EXPOSURE TO ADDITIONAL TAX LIABILITIES MAY ADVERSELY AFFECT OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: escalated
evidence: Many countries have adopted new tax laws to align with the global minimum tax.
reason: Last year said various countries had adopted or planned to adopt such laws; this year states many have adopted them, so the exposure is now more concretely realised. Other changes are dropped factors or rewording.

title: CLIMATE CHANGE, NATURAL DISASTERS, OR OTHER EVENTS BEYOND OUR CONTROL COULD DISRUPT OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Advocates and opponents of various ESG matters are increasingly turning to activism, including litigation or media campaigns, to advance their positions.
reason: The filing adds litigation and activism-driven ESG risk and conflicting anti-ESG policymaker actions, which last year's text did not cover, while dropping the CSRD example and the low-risk PG&E outage statement.

title: COMPLYING WITH FDA AND FOREIGN REGULATIONS IS A COMPLEX PROCESS, AND OUR FAILURE TO FULLY COMPLY COULD SUBJECT US TO SIGNIFICANT ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS.
label: new_exposure
evidence: In the EU, subject to the transitional provisions and in order to sell our products in EU member states, our products must comply with the general safety and performance requirements of the EU MDR
reason: The EU MDR creates a new source of loss: non-compliance could block CE marking and prevent EU sales, which last year's risk factor did not address.

title: OUR PRODUCTS ARE SUBJECT TO A LENGTHY AND UNCERTAIN DOMESTIC REGULATORY REVIEW PROCESS. IF WE DO NOT OBTAIN AND MAINTAIN THE NECESSARY DOMESTIC REGULATORY AUTHORIZATIONS, WE WILL NOT BE ABLE TO SELL OUR PRODUCTS IN THE U.S.
label: escalated
evidence: on February 2, 2026, the FDA’s final rule implementing the QMSR became effective
reason: The QMSR, already in exposure last year as a future rule, is now effective, with FDA stating ISO 13485 certification alone will not ensure compliance and adding new obligations.

title: OUR PRODUCTS ARE SUBJECT TO INTERNATIONAL REGULATORY PROCESSES AND APPROVAL OR CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS. IF WE DO NOT OBTAIN AND MAINTAIN THE NECESSARY REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS, WE WILL NOT BE ABLE TO SELL OUR PRODUCTS IN OTHER COUNTRIES.
label: boilerplate
evidence: on December 16, 2025, the European Commission published a targeted revision proposal of the EU MDR
reason: EU medical device regulatory change was already flagged last year; the proposal is a pending, non-final revision that does not add a new source of loss or show harm to the company.

title: CHANGES IN HEALTHCARE LEGISLATION AND POLICY MAY HAVE AN ADVERSE EFFECT ON OUR BUSINESS, FINANCIAL CONDITION, OR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.
label: new_exposure
evidence: implementation of OBBBA may reduce the number of individuals enrolled in state Medicaid programs and ACA marketplace plans
reason: A new federal law, OBBBA, is cited as a source of reduced enrollment and lower demand for the company's products, a risk last year's text did not cover.

title: IF WE ARE UNABLE TO FULLY PROTECT AND SUCCESSFULLY DEFEND OUR INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY FROM USE BY THIRD PARTIES, OUR ABILITY TO COMPETE MAY BE HARMED.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Notwithstanding our efforts to protect our intellectual property, our competitors may independently develop similar or alternative technologies or products that are equal to or superior to our technologies without infringing any of our intellectual property
reason: This year's text drops the risk that competitors may independently develop equal or superior non-infringing technologies, a material driver of competitive harm, so the risk is narrowed.

title: OTHERS MAY BE SUCCESSFUL IN ASSERTING THAT OUR PRODUCTS INFRINGE THEIR INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, WHICH MAY CAUSE US TO PAY SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGES AND/OR ENJOIN US FROM COMMERCIALIZING OUR PRODUCTS.
label: boilerplate
evidence: We cannot be certain that patents issued from our own patent applications covering our products will have a priority date over any patents issued from applications filed by a third party.
reason: Changes are rewording and reordering of existing risk language; last year's text already covered the same priority-date and invalidity uncertainties, and the removed sentences were not material drivers.

title: OUR FUTURE OPERATING RESULTS MAY BE BELOW EXPECTATIONS, WHICH COULD CAUSE OUR STOCK PRICE TO DECLINE.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Due to the dynamic nature of our industry, we have limited insight into trends that may emerge and affect our business.
reason: Changes are rewording and minor wording shifts (nascent to dynamic, removing 'market acceptance' qualifier, 'may' to 'could'); no new exposure or substantive change in risk.

title: OUR STOCK PRICE HAS BEEN, AND WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO BE, VOLATILE.
label: boilerplate
evidence: during 2025, the adjusted closing price of our common stock reached a high of $610.45 and a low of $429.59
reason: Only the price range figures were updated and the analyst-recommendation driver was reworded; the stock price risk and its drivers are substantively unchanged.

title: Weakening economic conditions in markets in which Linde does business may adversely impact its financial results and/or cash flows.
label: boilerplate
evidence: such as the chemicals and energy, and metals and mining end markets
reason: Only rewording of the cyclical industry list; the same industries are named with no change in exposure or substance.

title: Catastrophic events could disrupt the operations of Linde and/or its customers and suppliers and may have a significant adverse impact on the results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: natural disasters linked to climate change
reason: The risk is now explicitly tied to climate change and adds asset impairments as a new consequence, a larger cost than last year's text described.

title: Linde may be subject to information technology system failures, network disruptions and cybersecurity breaches or other related incidents.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including systems that utilize advanced technologies
reason: Added wording about advanced technology systems and cyber attacks/disruptions is rewording; the same exposures and no change in stated impact or likelihood.

title: Linde is subject to a variety of international laws and government regulations and changes in, or failure to comply with, these laws or regulations could have an adverse impact on the company’s business, financial position and results of operations.
label: boilerplate
evidence: data protection including artificial intelligence
reason: The list is reordered and two list items are expanded with AI and reporting wording, but the regulatory exposures and consequences are unchanged in substance.

title: Pharmaceutical research and development is very costly and highly uncertain; we may not succeed in developing, licensing, or acquiring commercially successful products sufficient in number or value to replace revenues of products that have lost or will lose intellectual property protection or are displaced by competing products or therapies.
label: escalated
evidence: after we and others may have attributed significant value for these potential products
reason: The risk now explicitly covers failures after significant value has been attributed to candidates, and adds diligence gaps and unanticipated investment costs, raising the likely size of losses.

title: We and our products face intense competition, and such competition could have a material adverse effect on our business.
label: new_exposure
evidence: faces intensifying competition worldwide, including from China and other markets where research and development capabilities have expanded and accelerated significantly
reason: Competition from China and other markets with expanded R&D capabilities is newly named; last year's text covered no such geographic source of competition.

title: Our business is subject to government price controls and other public and private restrictions on pricing, reimbursement, and access for our drugs, which could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, reputation, or business.
label: new_exposure
evidence: In November 2025, we announced preliminary voluntary agreements with the U.S. government
reason: New U.S. government pricing agreements, international price benchmarking and cash-pay obesity access risks are new sources of revenue loss not covered last year.

title: We derive a significant percentage of our total revenue from relatively few products and sell our products through consolidated supply chain entities, which subjects us to various risks.
label: escalated
evidence: For example, in July 2025, CVS Caremark, the pharmacy benefit management division of CVS Health, stopped covering Zepbound as a preferred obesity management medicine on some insurance plans, which has negatively impacted access for patients covered under these plans.
reason: The same PBM formulary exposure now shows a concrete materialised harm, a major PBM dropping Zepbound coverage and hurting patient access; concentration also rose from 48% to 56%.

title: We depend on products with intellectual property protection for most of our revenues, cash flows, and earnings; the loss of effective intellectual property protection for certain of our products has resulted, and in the future is likely to continue to result, in rapid and severe declines in revenues for those products.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Patent expirations of competitive products may also shift market conditions for our products by contracting the market for branded products, impacting product access, or otherwise intensifying pricing pressures across similar treatments.
reason: Competitors' patent expirations are now flagged as a new source of market contraction and pricing pressure on the company's products, which last year's text did not cover.

title: Our long-term success depends on intellectual property protection; if our intellectual property rights are invalidated, circumvented, or weakened, our business will be adversely affected.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Intellectual property threats across international markets include policies which favor domestic competitors or are otherwise disadvantageous to our products, challenges to our patents' validity in foreign courts, and government policies that force technology transfer
reason: New risk sources appear: discriminatory domestic-favoring policies, foreign court validity challenges, and forced technology transfer, none covered in last year's text.

title: Failure, inadequacy, breach of, or unauthorized access to, our IT systems or those of our third-party service providers, unauthorized access to our confidential information, or violations of data protection laws, could result in material harm to our business and reputation.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Third-party access to our proprietary data may also enable such party's development of competing products or enhancement of services sold to competitors, thereby eroding our competitive advantage.
reason: Adds a distinct loss path: authorized third-party access to proprietary data enabling competing products, not only breaches, eroding competitive advantage.

title: Manufacturing, quality, or supply chain difficulties, disruptions, or shortages could lead to product supply problems or other negative outcomes.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Relevant external environmental factors include (i) tariffs
reason: Tariffs are newly named as a cost and supply-disruption driver, a source of loss the prior text did not cover, though cost inflation and logistics were already cited.

title: Reliance on third-party relationships and outsourcing arrangements could adversely affect our business.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Tariffs have been imposed or proposed on a variety of other geographies in which we have third-party suppliers.
reason: Extends tariff cost and supply-disruption exposure beyond China to other countries where the company has third-party suppliers, which last year's text did not cover.

title: Our use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other emerging technologies could adversely impact us.
label: new_exposure
evidence: AI may enable new competitors in drug discovery and enhance the capabilities of existing competitors, thereby broadening and intensifying competitive dynamics.
reason: This year adds competition from AI-enabled new entrants and intensified rivalry as a source of loss not covered last year; competition was previously absent from the list of AI-exacerbated risks.

title: Our global operations subject us to risks, including as related to uneven economic growth or downturns, international trade, and other global disruptions, geopolitical tensions, or disputes.
label: new_exposure
evidence: disagreements with authorities regarding tariff classifications, transfer pricing, or valuations
reason: Transfer pricing and customs valuation disputes with authorities are new sources of loss not covered in last year's risk factor.

title: Changes in foreign currency rates, interest rate risks, and inflation or deflation affect our results of operations.
label: de_escalated
evidence: with some of these higher expenses due in part to policy actions intended to curb inflation
reason: Last year's text cited policy actions against inflation as a driver of higher expenses; this year's text drops that driver, while the new supply-chain and international-growth sentence adds a cause of an already-covered FX exposure.

title: We are party to litigation and investigations, which could adversely affect our business.
label: new_exposure
evidence: initiated enforcement or other actions across industries to seek alignment with policy initiatives
reason: Enforcement against the company to align with policy initiatives is a new legal risk source not covered last year, though the self-insurance scope change also warrants note.

title: We are subject to evolving and complex tax laws, which may result in additional liabilities.
label: escalated
evidence: the ultimate outcome of any tax matters may result in liabilities that are greater than amounts accrued in our estimates for uncertain tax positions
reason: The same tax-examination exposure now explicitly warns that liabilities could exceed reserves, a larger potential cost than last year's text described.

title: Regulatory compliance problems could be damaging to the company.
label: new_exposure
evidence: novel regulatory or policy programs such as the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher Pilot Program may attract scrutiny and criticism from various stakeholders
reason: Participation in the new FDA voucher pilot program is a newly named source of legal, political and reputational risk that last year's text did not mention.

title: We depend heavily on contracts with the U.S. Government for a substantial portion of our business. Changes in the U.S. Government’s priorities, or delays or reductions in spending could have a material adverse effect on our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Department of War (DoW), also known as the Department of Defense under 10 U.S.C. § 111(a)
reason: Changes are a renamed defined term, a slightly lower percentage, and reworded shutdown language with no new source of loss or shift in substance.</br>

title: The F-35 program comprises a material portion of our revenue and reductions or delays in funding for this program and risks related to performance, schedule, cost and requirements of the program could adversely affect our performance.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We may face similar risks for other complex and technologically advanced programs.
reason: The new sentence extends the program-specific risk to other complex, technologically advanced programs that last year's text did not cover. The F-35 'would' to 'may' softening is a secondary point.

title: Undefinitized Contract Action (UCA).
label: boilerplate
evidence: From time to time, we perform work under a UCA with the U.S. Government
reason: Rewording and condensing with the same substance; the unilateral definitization right and its profit and cash flow effects are unchanged, so no materiality change.

title: Competition and changing customer procurement policies could adversely affect our business and financial results.
label: de_escalated
evidence: We are facing increased competition from new entrants, startups and non-traditional defense contractors.
reason: The prior text said startups were favored by procurement policy, a material competitive driver now dropped, though the new proposed DoW acquisition reforms partly offset this.

title: We are heavily dependent on suppliers and if our subcontractors or other suppliers or teaming agreement or joint venture partners fail to perform their obligations, our performance and ability to win future business could be adversely affected.
label: boilerplate
evidence: could adversely affect their ability to meet their performance obligations and result in an impact on our business and results of operations
reason: Changes are rewording and minor deletions, such as dropping 'under the terms of most of our contracts'; the risk's substance and scope are unchanged.

title: Our success depends, in part, on our ability to develop new technologies, products and services and efficiently produce and deliver existing products.
label: new_exposure
evidence: if stakeholders perceive our company as being slow to adapt, lacking in innovation or inconsistently delivering results
reason: The risk now covers lost contracts from stakeholder perception of slowness or inconsistent delivery, a trigger the prior text did not name; the other edits are wording changes.

title: Geopolitical, macroeconomic and public health events and conditions could adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Government actions relating to rare earth minerals that are used in certain of our products, including U.S. Government sourcing prohibitions on the import of such minerals and the imposition of export controls on such minerals by China, have raised concerns about supply availability.
reason: Rare earth mineral supply disruption is a new source of loss not covered last year; the company now warns supply availability is vulnerable and could hurt profits and cash flows.

title: We may be unable to benefit fully from or adequately protect our intellectual property rights or use third-party intellectual property, which could negatively affect our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The DoW is also implementing an overarching intellectual property acquisition policy
reason: Changes are renamed department (DoD to DoW), wording tweaks like 'technical data' and reordering; no change in substance of the exposure.

title: Our business and financial performance depends on us identifying, attracting and retaining a highly skilled workforce.
label: boilerplate

evidence: the labor environment has experienced shifts that pose higher risk of future labor disruption
