title: As a U.S. government contractor, we are subject to risks relating to U.S. government audits, investigations, and disputes.
label: boilerplate
evidence: in October 2024, the Company entered into a deferred prosecution agreement and a civil settlement agreement with the DOJ
reason: The only substantive wording change is 'certain deferred prosecution agreements' becoming 'a deferred prosecution agreement', and the paragraph was reordered. The company does not say the exposure shrank.

title: A violation by Raytheon Company or the Company of any one of the deferred prosecution agreements or Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) administrative order announced on October 16, 2024 could adversely affect our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: A single independent compliance monitor was selected to oversee Raytheon Company’s and the Company’s compliance
reason: Changes reflect procedural updates, such as the monitor being selected and the charge wording being made more specific. The core breach risk and consequences are unchanged.

title: Our business and financial performance may be adversely affected by climate change, including regulations, customer demand, technologies, and extreme weather.
label: de_escalated
evidence: we continue to evaluate making additional investments in new technologies and capabilities
reason: The company now says it is evaluating rather than making additional investments, and customer and investor focus is described as possible rather than settled, softening the exposure.

title: Quarterly cash dividends and share repurchases are subject to uncertainties and may affect our common stock price.
label: new_exposure
evidence: pursuant to a January 7, 2026 Executive Order, the Secretary of War could seek to limit our ability to pay cash dividends or make share repurchases
reason: A new government executive order now allows the Secretary of War to restrict dividends and buybacks based on contract performance, a source of capital-return limitation not covered last year.

title: We may be unable to realize expected benefits from strategic initiatives.
label: boilerplate
evidence: We also use our Customer Oriented Results and Excellence (CORE) operating system
reason: Changes are rewording and dropping the 'realigned segment' and 'Industry 4.0' references; the exposure and its drivers are substantively unchanged.

title: Failure to successfully manage and execute potential future acquisitions, investments, divestitures, joint ventures, and other transactions, and other risks associated with these activities could adversely affect our future financial results.
label: de_escalated
evidence: In particular, if we are unable to complete the pending divestiture of Collins’ actuation and flight controls business within our expected timeframe or at all, we may be unable to reduce our outstanding debt according to planned timeframes.
reason: The prior-year warning about the pending Collins divestiture delaying debt reduction was dropped, a material driver, while the generic execution-timing risk was added in its place.

title: We may not be successful in implementing important strategic initiatives (including our restructuring plans), effectively managing growth, or executing strategic transactions, any of which may have an adverse impact on our business and financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: transitions to licensed or joint venture operating models
reason: New risk from transitions to licensed or joint venture models and JV management failures, plus a comparability risk from divestitures, portfolio actions and restructurings, were absent last year.

title: Evolving consumer preferences and tastes, as well as adverse public or medical opinions about the health effects of consuming our products, may adversely affect our business.
label: escalated
evidence: such as widespread use of targeted weight-loss medications
reason: Weight-loss drugs were already a named driver last year, but the text now describes their use as widespread, suggesting the exposure is larger and already occurring.

title: If our business partners and third-party providers do not satisfactorily fulfill their responsibilities and commitments, it could damage our brand, and our financial results could suffer.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We also rely on third-party service providers to perform certain business processes, and failures in the performance, oversight, or integration of these outsourced activities could adversely affect our operations, financial reporting, or internal controls.
reason: This year's text adds outsourced business-process providers, a source of operational and internal-control loss not covered last year, so it is a new exposure.

title: If we are unable to meet our projections for new coffeehouse openings or efficiently maintain the attractiveness of our existing coffeehouses, our operating results could suffer.
label: boilerplate
evidence: new coffeehouse openings or efficiently maintain the attractiveness of our existing coffeehouses
reason: Only the defined store term was renamed to coffeehouse; the risks, costs, and drivers are substantively unchanged.

title: We are highly dependent on the financial performance of our North America operating segment.
label: escalated
evidence: which accounted for approximately 76% of total net revenues in fiscal 2026
reason: Same North America dependence risk, but its revenue share rose from 74% to 76%, so the concentration exposure grew somewhat.

title: We are dependent on the performance of licensed and company-owned international markets to achieve our growth targets.
label: boilerplate
evidence: The International segment is an important profit center.
reason: Changes are wording tweaks (critical to important, grammar) with the same risk factors and no change in substance.

title: Increases in the cost of high-quality arabica coffee beans or other commodities or decreases in the availability of high-quality arabica coffee beans or other commodities could have an adverse impact on our business operations and financial results.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Changes in applicable tariffs have also affected, and in the future may affect, our costs to procure coffee.
reason: The added matcha, cups and lids, and the 'Changes in applicable tariffs' wording are examples or rewording of commodity exposures already covered; no change in substance.

title: Our financial condition and results of operations have been, and may continue to be, adversely affected by a number of macroeconomic and other factors, many of which are largely outside our control.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Extreme weather events and longer-term changes in weather patterns that impact consumers’ behaviors or the costs and availability of inputs in our products
reason: Climate-related weather risk was already listed last year; the change adds a demand channel and drops the named tax act, with no change in the size of exposure.

title: Failure to meet market expectations for our financial performance or any announced guidance will likely adversely affect the market price and increase the volatility of our stock, and fluctuations in the stock market as a whole may also impact the market price and volatility of our stock.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Any changes to, suspension of, or failure to meet investor expectations regarding our dividends or share repurchases may increase the volatility or affect the market price of our stock.
reason: The new dividend and buyback sentence restates shareholder-returns expectations already listed last year; only 'Back to Starbucks plan' was renamed to 'strategy', so substance is unchanged.

title: The loss of key personnel, difficulties with recruiting and retaining qualified personnel, or ineffectively managing changes in our workforce could adversely impact our business and financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: our performance depends on our ability, and the ability of our licensees and franchisees, to recruit and retain high-quality management personnel
reason: Recruiting risk now extends to licensee and franchisee workforces, a third-party counterparty source the prior text did not cover; the coffeehouse rename and AI mention are otherwise boilerplate.

title: Changes in the availability and cost of labor could adversely affect our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Changes in labor regulations could have a significant impact on the classification of employees as being exempt from overtime
reason: The change replaces specific federal and state examples with generic language and renames stores as coffeehouses; the exposure to labor regulation and union-related harm is substantively unchanged.

title: We face intense competition in each of our channels and markets, which could lead to reduced profitability.
label: boilerplate
evidence: convenience (including delivery, mobile ordering, speed of service, personalization and digital engagement), value perception, and price
reason: Expanded examples of competitive factors and renamed store references reflect rewording only; the competitive exposure itself is unchanged in substance.

title: Climate change may have an adverse impact on our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Operating in 91 global markets
reason: Changes are an updated market count, wording tweaks and 'stores' to 'coffeehouses'; the same exposure is described with no change in substance or magnitude.

title: Our business is subject to evolving regulatory and stakeholder demands and expectations, including with respect to responsible business matters, that could expose us to numerous risks.
label: new_exposure
evidence: activist campaigns can result in significant costs, including legal expenses and diversion of management and Board attention
reason: This year adds a new risk from shareholder activism, covering costs, strategic uncertainty, stock volatility, and large-holder influence, which last year's text did not address.

title: Failure to comply with applicable laws and changing legal and regulatory requirements could harm our business and financial results.
label: escalated
evidence: changes in U.S. and foreign tax laws, including global minimum tax regimes, may increase compliance costs, create uncertainty, or adversely affect our effective tax rate, cash flows, or results of operations.
reason: Last year Pillar Two was expected to be immaterial; this year tax law changes are flagged as a potential adverse hit to tax rate and cash flows, a higher-impact framing of the same exposure.

title: The unauthorized access, use, theft, or destruction of customer or employee data (personal, financial, or other), or of Starbucks proprietary or confidential information, that is stored in our information systems or by third parties could impact our reputation and brand and expose us to potential liability and loss of revenues.
label: escalated
evidence: including artificial-intelligence-enabled social engineering, automated reconnaissance, credential attacks, and impersonation techniques
reason: The same AI-driven cyber threat is now described with more specific attack methods, signalling a larger and more sophisticated threat than last year's generic language, though no new source of loss is introduced.

title: Failure to maintain satisfactory compliance with certain privacy and data protection laws and regulations may result in substantial negative financial consequences, reputational harm, and civil or criminal penalties.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including U.S. national security regulations on customer and partner data
reason: The added national security data rules fall within the existing general coverage of national privacy laws. The Starbucks Digital Solutions example was dropped, but the underlying exposure is unchanged.

title: We rely heavily on information technology in our operations and growth initiatives, and any material failure, inadequacy, interruption, or security failure of that technology could harm our ability to effectively operate and grow our business and could adversely affect our financial results.
label: boilerplate
evidence: changes to our mobile order, loyalty, delivery integration, or payment systems
reason: The added system changes and prolonged outages are new framings of failure modes already covered by outages, software flaws, and misconfigurations, so no new source of loss is introduced.

title: Failure to adequately protect our intellectual property or ensure that we are not infringing on the intellectual property of others could harm the value of our brand and our business.
label: boilerplate
evidence: Securing and enforcing intellectual property rights across markets and technologies can be costly and time-consuming.
reason: Changes are minor wording additions (across markets and technologies, time consuming to defend, avoid infringement or a claim of infringement) with no change in the underlying exposure.

title: Developments in the business, economic, and geopolitical environment could negatively impact our business.
label: escalated
evidence: Market-driven changes, such as declines in equity markets, can also reduce client demand for margin lending, which is a significant source of net interest revenue.
reason: Adds a new concrete channel (reduced margin lending demand from equity declines) tied to a major revenue source, but it is the same general market exposure already covered, so it is not a new source of loss.

title: A significant change in client cash allocations could negatively impact our income.
label: boilerplate
evidence: the Company utilized higher-cost supplemental funding sources
reason: Changes are rewording and emphasis only: 'extensively' versus 'supplemental' and an added 'For example' lead-in; the same exposure and history are described with no change in substance.

title: Significant interest rate changes could affect our profitability.
label: new_exposure
evidence: as well as margin loans, mortgages, and PALs
reason: Margin loans and PALs are newly named interest-earning assets, adding credit and rate exposure that last year's text did not cover.

title: A significant decrease in our liquidity could negatively affect our business as well as reduce client confidence in us.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Larger unrealized losses on our available for sale (AFS) portfolio due to higher market interest rates negatively impact our capital position inclusive of AOCI, including our tangible capital.
reason: This year's text drops the AFS unrealized-loss and tangible-capital constraint on FHLB access, a material funding driver, while adding secured funding sources that soften the liquidity risk.

title: Security breaches of our systems, or those of our clients or third parties, may subject us to significant liability and damage our reputation.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Losses reimbursed to clients under our guarantee against unauthorized account activity could have a negative impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
reason: This year's text drops the paragraph on external fraud using stolen client credentials and the losses from the account-activity guarantee, a material driver of loss, without saying the exposure shrank.

title: Technology and operational failures or errors and other operational risks could subject us to losses, litigation, regulatory actions, and reputational damage.
label: boilerplate
evidence: dealers, custodians, and other intermediaries to which client orders are routed
reason: Custodians are added to a list already covered by 'other intermediaries'; the date update and dropped fraud paragraph do not change the substance of the exposure.

title: We rely on outsourced service providers and financial intermediaries to perform key functions, and failure of these entities to perform as expected could result in financial or reputational harm to us or financial harm to our clients.
label: new_exposure
evidence: We rely on market makers, dealers, securities exchanges, clearing houses, custodians, and other financial intermediaries to execute and settle our clients’ orders.
reason: Reliance on market makers, exchanges, clearing houses and dealers for order execution and settlement, plus collateral custody risk, is new; last year's text did not cover these intermediaries.

title: Legislation or changes in rules and regulations could negatively affect our business and financial results.
label: new_exposure
evidence: and digital assets may directly affect our operations and profitability or our specific business lines
reason: This year adds digital assets, including cryptocurrency trading, as a new regulated business line with pending rules that could hurt profitability, a source of loss not covered last year.

title: Potential strategic transactions could have a negative impact on our financial position.
label: new_exposure
evidence: including our acquisition of Forge, could have a material impact on our financial position
reason: The named Forge acquisition is new and specific; it adds a concrete pending transaction source of risk that last year's generic risk text did not cover.

title: Southern Company and its subsidiaries are subject to substantial federal, state, and local governmental regulation, including with respect to rates. The reduction, elimination, or expiration of government incentives for, or regulations mandating or restricting the use of, renewable energy projects could reduce demand for renewable energy projects and harm the Registrants' businesses.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The OBBB, among other things, materially changed the requirements for most of the federal renewable energy incentives.
reason: The OBBB and loss or reduction of renewable tax incentives is a new source of potential material adverse effect not covered last year, and the company says impacts are still being assessed.

title: The Southern Company system may be exposed to regulatory and financial risks related to the impact of GHG legislation, regulation, and emission reduction goals.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The public holds diverse and often conflicting views on the use of fossil fuels which may subject the Registrants to adverse publicity in connection with their use or supply of fossil fuels.
reason: New reputational risk from adverse publicity over fossil fuel use, not covered last year. Ranks above the escalated 2030 goal change, which is also material.

title: The financial performance of Southern Company and its subsidiaries may be adversely affected if the subsidiaries are unable to successfully operate their facilities or perform certain corporate functions.
label: new_exposure
evidence: failure of performance by counterparties
reason: Counterparty nonperformance is newly listed as a source of operational risk, a distinct loss driver not named in last year's text, though related third-party risks were covered.

title: Generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity and transportation and storage of natural gas involve risks that may result in accidents and other operating risks and costs and that may present potential exposures in excess of insurance coverage.
label: boilerplate
evidence: natural gas pipelines, storage facilities, and other infrastructure are subject to various state and other regulatory requirements
reason: Changes are rewording and broadening of infrastructure wording with no new hazard, exposure, or change in penalty risk described.

title: An information security incident, including a cybersecurity breach, or the failure of, or inability to remotely access, one or more key technology systems, networks, or processes could impact the ability of the Registrants to operate.
label: escalated
evidence: Use of generative artificial intelligence has also increased the frequency, scale, and sophistication of cyber attacks and increased the capability of less sophisticated actors.
reason: AI-enabled attacks were previously only a hypothetical future risk; the filing now says generative AI is already increasing attack frequency, scale, and sophistication, a risk already materialising within a covered exposure.

title: The Southern Company system may not be able to obtain adequate natural gas, fuel supplies, and other resources required to operate the traditional electric operating companies' and Southern Power's electric generating plants or serve Southern Company Gas' natural gas customers.
label: new_exposure
evidence: constraints on existing natural gas pipeline capacity or on construction of new natural gas pipelines, or changing economic conditions
reason: The fuel-disruption list now names pipeline capacity and construction constraints and changing economic conditions, which last year's text did not cite as causes of supply loss.

title: The Subsidiary Registrants are subject to workforce factors that could affect operations.
label: de_escalated
evidence: continuing workforce trends occurring in the United States triggered by decisions of employees to leave the workforce
reason: This year's text drops last year's discussion of continuing attrition trends and competition from remote-work employers, a material driver of workforce risk, so the risk is narrower.

title: Supply chain disruptions, inflation, elevated interest rates, trade policies (including tariffs and other trade measures), and other economic factors could negatively impact operations.
label: escalated
evidence: Supply chain disruptions and trade policies have contributed to higher prices of components, materials, equipment, and other needed commodities
reason: Tariffs were already covered, but the text now says trade policies have already contributed to higher prices and extends the risk to other trade measures, so the exposure is more concrete.

title: The Registrants have incurred and may incur additional costs or delays in the construction of new plants or other facilities and may not be able to recover their investments. Also, existing facilities of the Subsidiary Registrants require ongoing expenditures, including those to maintain reliability and meet AROs and other environmental standards and goals.
label: escalated
evidence: the pace and extent of the traditional electric operating companies' planned construction program have increased
reason: The construction program is larger than last year, and the company now says traditional electric operating companies are already incurring significant engineering, design, and equipment costs that may be lost on cancellation.

title: Southern Company Gas' significant investment in pipeline development projects involves financial and execution risks.
label: escalated
evidence: and Southern Company Gas may participate in other pipeline development projects in the future
reason: The same pipeline-development risk now extends to possible future projects, enlarging the potential capital exposure, though the category was already covered by the title and prior text.

title: The electric generation and energy marketing operations of the traditional electric operating companies and Southern Power and the natural gas operations of Southern Company Gas are subject to changes in energy prices and fuel costs.
label: boilerplate
evidence: increased demand for natural gas, including to fuel electric generation to serve data centers and other large load customers
reason: The added data-center demand driver is a new cause of the same gas price volatility already disclosed, not a new source of loss; other edits are wording only.

title: The Registrants are subject to risks associated with a changing economic environment, customer behaviors, including increased energy conservation, and adoption patterns of technologies by customers.
label: new_exposure
evidence: elimination of government energy assistance programs, government shutdowns, increases in energy prices
reason: Loss of government energy assistance and government shutdowns are newly named drivers of reduced customer consumption, a source of lower sales not cited last year.

title: The operating results of the Registrants are affected by weather conditions and may fluctuate on a seasonal basis. In addition, catastrophic events could result in substantial damage to or limit the operation of the properties of a Subsidiary Registrant.
label: escalated
evidence: Any such delay or failure in recovering costs by the Subsidiary Registrants could have a material adverse effect on the Registrants, including lower credit ratings and, thus, higher costs for future debt issuances
reason: Adds an explicit material adverse effect from storm cost recovery delays, including lower credit ratings, higher debt costs, and limits on funding capital expenditures, a larger consequence than last year's text described.

title: Uncertainty in demand for energy can result in lower earnings or higher costs.
label: new_exposure
evidence: these industries may experience a business downturn, which could cause the loss of current or potential customers or may weaken the financial condition and creditworthiness of existing customers
reason: This year's text adds counterparty credit risk from data center and industrial customers, which last year's text did not cover; the increased concentration in one industry is also new.

title: The businesses of the Registrants and Nicor Gas are dependent on their ability to successfully access capital through capital markets and financial institutions.

evidence: affordability concerns from increased borrowing costs could require the Registrants and Nicor Gas, unilaterally or at the direction of their regulators, to significantly scale back infrastructure investment, which could lead to additional risks related to safety and reliability
reason: The same capital-access exposure now carries a new concrete harm chain: borrowing-cost affordability could force infrastructure scale-backs and raise safety and reliability risks.

title: Failure to comply with debt covenants or conditions could adversely affect the ability of the Registrants, SEGCO, Southern Company Gas Capital, or Nicor Gas to execute future borrowings.
label: new_exposure
evidence: Future debt and credit agreements may contain additional or different covenants, events of default, and mandatory prepayment events.
reason: Adds a new source of risk from future agreements with unknown covenants, which last year's text did not cover; this is a material expansion of covenant exposure.

title: Conditions that adversely affect the general retail environment could materially and adversely affect us.
label: escalated
evidence: implemented and threatened tariffs, retaliatory tariffs and trade disputes

evidence: we may face construction delays or higher construction costs caused by potential increases in the cost of imported goods and materials due to threatened or implemented tariffs and international trade disputes
reason: Tariffs and international trade disputes are a new source of construction cost and delay risk not covered in any form last year.

title: Disruption in the capital and credit markets may increase the cost of capital and may adversely affect our ability to access external financings for our growth and ongoing debt service requirements.
label: de_escalated
evidence: Additionally, a high interest rate environment, could prevent us from accessing capital at attractive interest rates
reason: The company dropped its statement that high rates are current and expected to continue in 2025, and added free cash flow as a funding source, reducing reliance on external financing.

title: We have limited control with respect to some properties that are partially owned or managed by third parties, which may adversely affect our ability to sell or refinance them.
label: escalated
evidence: we owned interests in 110 income-producing properties with other parties
reason: The count of jointly owned properties rose from 99 to 110, and international joint venture properties rose from 24 to 29, so exposure to shared-control assets grew.

title: Artificial generative intelligence technologies present risks related to the control of our proprietary business information, keeping such information confidential, and emerging regulatory risk, any or all of which may adversely affect our business and results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: if we fail to adapt to changes from an increased use of AI
reason: New sentence notes competitors, retailers and consumers increasingly use AI, adding competitive-adaptation risk to an already-covered AI exposure; this is a heightened but not wholly new source of loss.

title: Our international activities may subject us to risks that are different from or greater than those associated with our domestic operations.
label: escalated
evidence: impact from threatened or implemented tariffs and international trade disputes
reason: Tariffs, now described as implemented as well as threatened, and added cost and inefficiency language suggest the same trade exposure is more likely and more costly than last year.

title: Inflationary pressures on costs, such as inputs for devices we sell and network components, labor and distribution costs, may impact our network construction, our financial condition or results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: Recent spending by hyperscalers and others to support AI is beginning to pressure supply chains for goods such as semiconductors and other network components.
reason: Supplier-capacity and raw-material demand pressures were already covered; the new AI-driven semiconductor pressure is described as already materialising, so it is escalated rather than a new source of loss.

title: Adverse changes in global financial markets could limit our ability and our larger customers’ and suppliers’ ability to access capital or increase the cost of capital needed to fund business operations.

evidence: A company’s cost of borrowing is affected by evaluations given by various credit rating agencies, and these agencies have been applying tighter credit standards when evaluating debt levels and future growth prospects.
reason: This year's text drops the credit rating agency tightening sentence, but the rating downgrade risk remains covered elsewhere, so no exposure shrank materially.

title: Industry-Wide Factors: Changes to federal, state and foreign government regulations and decisions in regulatory proceedings, as well as private litigation, could further increase our operating costs and/or alter customer perceptions of our operations, which could materially adversely affect us.

reason: This year's text adds state rate regulation of broadband as a regulatory cause, a source of cost not named last year; the FAA C-Band commitment was also dropped, which is a lesser point.

evidence: In 2023, the FCC’s statutory authority to conduct spectrum auctions lapsed and it is uncertain when Congress will act to reauthorize it.
reason: This year's text drops last year's discussion of the FCC auction authority lapse and the uncertain federal spectrum availability, a material driver of the spectrum risk.

evidence: In certain circumstances, we could be liable for the actions of our suppliers and other third parties we do business with.

title: We may not realize or sustain the expected benefits from acquisitions, joint ventures or our business transformation initiatives, including dispositions, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, operations, financial condition, results of operations and competitive position.
label: new_exposure
evidence: which may include acquisitions, joint ventures, particularly those aimed at enhancing our fiber serviceable locations, and other strategic transactions
reason: Acquisitions, joint ventures and dispositions are newly named as sources of benefit-realization risk, which last year's transformation-only risk factor did not cover.

title: Cyberattacks impacting our networks, systems or data or those of our suppliers or vendors may have a material adverse effect on our operations or results of operations.
label: escalated
evidence: Cyberattacks have caused, and may in the future cause, equipment or network failures, copying or loss of information
reason: The risk now states that cyberattacks have already caused network failures, data loss and expenses, not only that they could, showing the harm materialising.

title: Our business may be impacted by changes in tax laws and regulations, judicial interpretations of the same or administrative actions by federal, state, local and foreign taxing authorities.
label: boilerplate
evidence: the application of existing, newly enacted or amended tax laws may be uncertain

evidence: expanding our digital assortment through third-party sellers on our Target Plus marketplace
reason: Adds a named third-party marketplace business line, a source of risk the prior filing did not mention. The new-entrant competition language also adds a cause not previously covered.

title: If we do not anticipate consumer demand accurately and respond quickly to changing consumer preferences, our results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected.
label: boilerplate
evidence: We have not always been able to accurately forecast consumer demand or react to rapid changes in consumer preferences and spending patterns
reason: Wording changes only ('predict' to 'forecast', 'adapt' to 'react', condensed closing sentence); the same risk and prior impacts are described with no change in substance.

title: Our continued success is dependent on positive perceptions of Target which, if eroded, could adversely affect our business and our relationships, including with our guests, team members, and vendors.
label: escalated
evidence: as well as consumer boycotts organized throughout 2025
reason: The company now describes consumer boycotts that actually occurred throughout 2025, showing the DEI-initiative risk materialising with concrete harm rather than only a possibility.

title: If we are unable to protect against inventory shrink, our results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected.

evidence: In recent years, we have experienced elevated levels of inventory shrink relative to historical levels, which have adversely affected, and could continue to adversely affect, our results of operations and financial condition.
reason: This year's text drops last year's statement that shrink was elevated and had already hurt results, a material driver softening the disclosed exposure.

title: We depend on seasonal moments and higher-margin merchandise to drive sales and net earnings growth.
label: escalated
evidence: could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition to a greater degree
reason: The seasonality risk now carries a greater potential impact, and the higher-margin risk adds a gross margin rate decline, though the underlying exposures are unchanged.

title: If our capital investments do not achieve appropriate returns or our efficiency efforts are not successful, our competitive position, results of operations, and financial condition could be adversely affected.
label: de_escalated
evidence: We cannot guarantee that we will realize all of the potential cost savings from this initiative
reason: The enterprise-wide cost-savings initiative risk paragraph was dropped entirely this year, removing a material driver of adverse results, while other changes are minor additions.

title: Changes in our relationships with our vendors or other companies, changes in tax or trade policy, interruptions in our operations or supply chain, and increased commodity or supply chain costs could adversely affect our reputation and results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: The amount of duties and tariffs that we pay to import merchandise could rise substantially if the U.S. government eliminates the availability of the first sale declaration methodology
reason: The 10-K adds a first sale duty-methodology risk that last year's text did not cover, with potential substantial duty increases and possible Customs investigations.

title: If services we obtain from third parties are unavailable, fail to meet our standards, or increase in cost, our reputation, results of operations, and financial condition could be adversely affected.
label: new_exposure
evidence: including portions of our technology infrastructure (including certain generative artificial intelligence services)
reason: This year's text adds generative AI services and digital advertising offerings as third-party dependencies not covered last year, introducing new sources of service-failure loss.

title: We rely on a large, global, and changing workforce of team members, contractors, and temporary staffing. If we do not effectively manage our workforce, our labor costs and results of operations could be adversely affected.
label: boilerplate
evidence: the continuous advancements in automation and artificial intelligence capabilities will continue to impact the skills required in our workforce
reason: The added AI and automation sentence describes a skills-training pressure within the existing attract, train and retain workforce risk, with no new source of loss or harm stated. Dropping the executive-orders parenthetical is an example removal.

title: Failure to address product safety and sourcing concerns could adversely affect our results of operations.
label: boilerplate
evidence: including to diversify the geographic locations of our vendors to mitigate the impacts of tariffs or other trade policies
reason: Tariff-driven vendor diversification is a new example of an alternative-sourcing risk already covered; third-party sellers were already in last year's sourcing language, so substance is unchanged.

title: Our failure to comply with applicable laws, or changes in these laws, could adversely affect our reputation, results of operations, and financial condition.
label: new_exposure
evidence: including merchandise costs and availability, customs and trade policy (including the impacts of our first sale declaration program)
reason: This year adds customs and trade policy, including the first sale declaration program, as a named area of legal change; last year's text did not cover it, creating a new source of cost and loss.

title: Increases in our effective income tax rate could adversely affect our results of operations.
label: new_exposure
evidence: the continued availability of purchased tax credits
reason: Adds availability of purchased tax credits as a new driver of the effective tax rate, a source of exposure last year's text did not name.

title: Economic, political, foreign currency and other risks associated with international sales and operations could adversely affect our results of operations.
label: new_exposure
